source.description:
## PROBLEM

Install-order regressions surface late — usually at release time or on operators' fresh machines. The existing `fresh-machine-smoke.yml` runs on GH Actions ubuntu-latest which ships with Node, npm, python, curl, and dozens of other tools already. That masks bootstrap steps that would fail on a truly bare system. We have no reproducible harness that starts from "nothing but the OS image" and lands at "xt / sp / pi all functional, tests pass". Alpine is a good stress case because it's small, uses musl (not glibc), and lacks most preinstalled tooling.

## SUCCESS

Reproducible harness that:
1. Starts from `alpine:latest` (or a pinned tag) with nothing but base + apk
2. Installs the full runtime stack step by step, capturing every failure mode: system deps (bash, git, curl, python3, build-base for native compiles) → Node LTS via nvm or Alpine's own node package → bun (for `sp` which shebangs `bun`) → optionally rust for git-cliff if any repo still resolves it via cargo → pi (`@mariozechner/pi-coding-agent` or the fork we ship) → claude (the Claude Code CLI) → beads binary → xtrm-tools (`xt`) via npm global → specialists via `sp init`
3. Runs a broad smoke matrix: `xt init -y`, `xt doctor --json`, `xt update --apply`, `sp init`, `sp doctor`, `sp list`, `sp render-bead`, `pi --version`, `claude --version`, at least one xtmux command (`xtmux picker --dry-run`), and the workflows (a dry-run `xrm-release` and `xtrm-merge-fifo` at least).
4. Emits a diagnostic report (which step failed, what package was missing, exit code, tail of output) — should be trivially readable for someone triaging.
5. Runs in CI as a matrix leg alongside the existing ubuntu-latest smoke — not replacing it.

## SCOPE

- `.docker/alpine-install-smoke/` (new dir): Dockerfile + entrypoint script + expected-outcomes fixture + docs
- `.github/workflows/alpine-install-smoke.yml` (new): workflow_dispatch + optional pull_request trigger scoped to installer-surface changes (mirror `xtrm-xnf7g` selectivity)
- Docs: `docs/alpine-smoke.md` explaining the harness + how to run locally (`docker run` one-liner)
- Update `docs/release.md` §3 pre-flight section to include the alpine smoke

## NON_GOALS

- Not a full production runtime (musl + Alpine has real caveats — e.g., `@beads/bd` prebuilt binaries may not have musl variants). If a step is fundamentally not-alpine-compatible, document it as such rather than working around it.
- Not replacing ubuntu-latest fresh-machine-smoke — this is complementary.
- Not fixing every failure the harness surfaces — first pass just captures them.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Container must start from a bare Alpine image, no pre-built xtrm-tools image
- Every install command logged with stdout+stderr + exit code
- Report must be machine-readable JSON alongside human-readable log
- Reproducible: two identical runs produce identical reports modulo timestamps
- CI leg allowed to fail (surface findings without blocking release cadence) initially

## VALIDATION

- Local: `docker run --rm -v $PWD:/repo alpine-smoke-image` produces a report
- CI: workflow triggered on demand + on installer-surface PRs, uploads artifacts
- First run generates a real punch-list of things that don't work on musl / Alpine
- Report format is stable enough to diff run-over-run (regression detection)

## OUTPUT

Working Dockerfile + workflow + docs + initial punch-list report as artifacts of the first CI run. Follow-up beads filed for each real bug found.

## REFERENCES

- `docs/release.md` §3 (existing fresh-machine-smoke path)
- `.github/workflows/fresh-machine-smoke.yml` (the ubuntu-latest baseline)
- `.github/workflows/install-order-matrix.yml` (workflow_dispatch-only regression harness)
- `xtrm-5k0o` family (PATH cache bootstrap issues — likely relevant)
- `xtrm-xnf7g` (installer-surface PR gate — model for selective triggering)
source.title: Bare Alpine install-process investigation: full runtime bootstrap + broad tests
